function_question: How does nature stay cool without any power?

opening.text: There was a girl called Elena whose Grandma Rosa lived in a small house with a sunny garden.
Every afternoon, Elena visited Grandma Rosa after school, and they made lemonade and read stories together.
Summer came, and by the afternoon it was 35 °C inside! "An air conditioner is too noisy and costs too much to run," said Grandma. "Could my house cool itself?"

chapters.label: Chapter 1
chapters.title: The hottest afternoon
chapters.line: Elena fans Grandma and wonders: could the house cool itself, with no machine at all?

chapters.label: Chapter 2
chapters.title: Elena asks for help
chapters.line: Elena has lots of questions, and she needs a teammate. What about you?

chapters.label: Chapter 3
chapters.title: The nature heroes
chapters.line: You and Elena go exploring to meet animals that stay cool without any power.

chapters.label: Chapter 4
chapters.title: The secret of rising air
chapters.line: The heroes share the secret they all use.

chapters.label: Chapter 5
chapters.title: Training in the air lab
chapters.line: Every hero needs training. Elena shows you a mug of hot water and a tissue strip.

chapters.label: Chapter 5½
chapters.title: The why detective
chapters.line: Elena asks: why is Grandma's house so hot? Then she asks why again…

chapters.label: Chapter 6
chapters.title: The plan
chapters.line: Every cool house starts as a drawing.

chapters.label: Chapter 7
chapters.title: The big test
chapters.line: The first house is still too warm. You fix it, and try again.

chapters.label: Chapter 8
chapters.title: A breezy, quiet house
chapters.line: Grandma's house is breezy, quiet and cool.

guide.brief: I'm Popi, your story guide. Grandma Rosa's house gets far too hot, and she doesn't want a noisy air conditioner. Can you help Elena cool it down? Let's start!
guide.your_idea: Some engineers already have a spark of an idea. Do you?
guide.nature_clues: Nature solved this long ago. Tap each card to meet four nature heroes who stay cool with no power at all!
guide.design_secret: Here's the secret all four heroes share…
guide.skill: Scientists predict before they test. Where will the air be warmer? Ask an adult to help with the hot water.
guide.sketch: Time to draw Grandma's house cut in half like a dollhouse, like a real architect!
guide.build_and_test: Build your two shoebox houses and let's see how much cooler yours stays in the sun!
guide.retry_tip: Engineers never stop at round 1. Change ONE thing and test again!
guide.ending: And ever since then, Grandma Rosa's house cools itself with YOUR design. She sips lemonade in the breeze, and it's quiet enough to hear the birds!

quick_check.question: It's 35 °C inside Grandma's house. Your design cools it by 7 °C. What's the new temperature?
quick_check.right: Right! 35 − 7 = 28 °C. That's a big difference on a hot afternoon!
quick_check.wrong: Not quite. Cooler means take away: try 35 − 7.

clue_cards.name: Termites
clue_cards.trick: Mounds with a tall chimney and tunnels.
clue_cards.does: Warm air rises out of the top and pulls cooler air in lower down.

clue_cards.name: Prairie dogs
clue_cards.trick: Burrows with one raised entrance and one flat one.
clue_cards.does: Wind over the raised one pulls fresh air through the tunnel.

clue_cards.name: Elephant
clue_cards.trick: Huge, thin ears full of blood vessels.
clue_cards.does: Flapping them sheds heat into the air.

clue_cards.name: Desert snail
clue_cards.does: Reflects most of the sunlight, keeping the snail much cooler inside.

items.label: Cold air from an open freezer

predict.explain: Warm air is lighter than cool air, so it rises and cool air sinks. A low opening and a high one let this flow cool a house: the stack effect.

lab.title: The rising air lab
lab.predict: Where will the air be warmer?

tool.name: 5 Whys
tool.intro: 5 Whys is a detective tool. You ask "why?" again and again until you find the root cause. Sometimes there's more than one! Today you'll use all 5 whys.

parts.name: Why #1
parts.example: 🔦 Why won't the torch turn on? The battery is flat.
parts.starter: Why is Grandma's house so hot? Because…

parts.name: Why #2
parts.example: 🔦 Why is it flat? It was left on all night.
parts.starter: Why does the roof get so hot? Because…

parts.name: Why #3
parts.example: 🔦 Why was it left on? The switch got knocked in a bag.
parts.starter: Why does the hot air stay inside? Because…

parts.name: Why #4
parts.what: Keep digging: don't stop at the easy answer.
parts.example: 🔦 Why did it get knocked? The switch sticks out.
parts.starter: Why can't the hot air escape? Because…

parts.name: Why #5
parts.what: Reach the root cause, then fix that.
parts.example: 🔦 Root cause: the switch sticks out. Fix: a sunken switch!
parts.starter: Why is there no high vent? Because…

reflection.question: Which change cooled your house the most?
